title: Nvidia doubles down on Taiwan supply chain as AI squeezes substrate and OSAT capacity
content: Nvidia is deepening its ties with Taiwan's artificial intelligence supply chain by issuing capacity prepayments to fund expansion across IC substrates, advanced packaging, and testing—locking in production capacity for the next three to five years despite ongoing uncertainty over its CEO succession. The push comes as accelerating custom ASIC projects from cloud service providers and rival chipmakers intensify competition for scarce manufacturing capacity.

title: Nvidia maintains product roadmap as AI chip supply chain impact stays limited
content: Following Nvidia's latest earnings conference, the company's operating performance, outlook, and product development timeline showed no apparent impact from the departure of former CEO Jensen Huang. AI chip demand remains strong, although the company's financing policies are expected to become stricter than in the past.

title: ASE invests NT$248.9B in Renwu K52 plant for AI testing
content: Taiwan Fore Electronics, a subsidiary of ASE Technology Holding, will invest NT$248.9 billion (US$7.54 billion) in a new K52 plant at the J block of Kaohsiung's Renwu industrial park, with construction scheduled for phased completion in 2028 and 2029. Together, the K and J sites are expected to generate annual revenue of approximately NT$117.3 billion and create 3,300 jobs, expanding the area's advanced semiconductor testing cluster.

title: Tighter US chip rules set to favor Qualcomm and MediaTek
content: The US Department of Commerce has introduced stricter chip technology controls affecting China and several Southeast Asian and Latin American countries, requiring case-by-case approval for shipments of products built on processes below 16/14nm. The rules are expected to hurt Chinese chip designers while benefiting Qualcomm and MediaTek as alternative suppliers.

title: US AI curbs disrupt Southeast Asia shipments; MSI sees worst-case impact of one month
content: The recent US expansion of export controls on artificial intelligence (AI) products is rippling through the Southeast Asian operations of Taiwanese system integrators, as well as motherboard and graphics card makers. Micro-Star International (MSI) General Manager Chin-Ching Huang said some transactions in the region have been put on hold, estimating the worst-case operational impact at roughly one month.

title: Microsoft reaffirms Nvidia partnership after CEO departure
content: Microsoft's chief executive has expressed regret over the departure of Nvidia's chief executive while reaffirming confidence in the chipmaker and its partnership with Microsoft. The comments, reported by TechCrunch, followed the Nvidia board's decision and included support for the company's interim chief executive.

title: Intel lands first customer for 18A-P foundry process

title: MSI targets over 10% non-PC revenue with on-premises AI
content: Micro-Star International (MSI) is reshaping its product and operating structure as AI computing demand expands, export controls tighten, and rising memory prices pressure the PC market. President Jeans Huang said PC shipments are expected to contract in the first half of 2027, prompting MSI to pursue premium, high-value products and non-PC businesses while focusing its AI strategy on computing devices, edge computing, and enterprise on-premises applications.

title: Xi outlines four APEC cooperation pillars as trilateral talks with Trump, Putin draw focus
content: The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting opened in Shenzhen, China, on November 19, with Chinese President Xi Jinping proposing four pillars—trade, connectivity, innovation, and development—to deepen regional cooperation. Xi highlighted the digital economy, artificial intelligence, cross-border data flows, and clean energy as core priorities.

title: UBright eyes semiconductor, passive components and smart acoustics growth
content: As competition intensifies in the optical film market, UBright Optronics is accelerating its product and technology transformation. The company is expanding into semiconductor packaging and optical waveguides while investing in passive components and smart acoustics. It expects its new businesses to begin contributing revenue in 2027.

title: Samsung's silence on 2027 8-inch MPW plan worries South Korean IC design firms
content: Samsung Electronics' foundry division is gradually winding down its 8-inch process operations but has yet to announce its 2027 8-inch multi-project wafer (MPW) plan, raising concerns among South Korean IC design firms about losing access to trial production.

title: NCT builds capacity to commercialize gallium oxide with Mitsubishi Electric
content: Novel Crystal Technology (NCT), a Japan-based developer of gallium oxide (Ga₂O₃) wafers, is accelerating commercialization by building its own production capacity rather than adopting a fabless model. The company is also working with Mitsubishi Electric to develop materials for power semiconductors, aiming to submit materials for next-stage investment evaluation by the end of fiscal 2026 (April 2026–March 2027).
